title: Intermittent corruption in the session snapshot service

entities.description: Stores and retrieves serialized session snapshots
Optional payload compression before cache storage
Distributed cache used for snapshot payloads

evidence.text: At 14:10 UTC, snapshot read failures rose from 0.04% to 3.8% in two regions; affected reads reported checksum mismatches after cache retrieval.
Serializer version 3 had reached 50% of application instances at 13:55 UTC, while the compression flag had been raised from 20% to 80% of tenants at 14:00 UTC.
Database latency briefly increased from 18 ms to 41 ms during the alert, but database reads of the same affected snapshot IDs returned payloads whose checksums matched their stored metadata.
The cache fleet reported no evictions, host replacements, or memory-error alarms during the incident window.
Failures were concentrated among payloads larger than 64 KiB, although 91% of all snapshots larger than 64 KiB were read successfully.
For tenants with compression disabled, checksum failure rates were 0.05% on serializer version 2 and 0.06% on serializer version 3.
For tenants with compression enabled, checksum failure rates were 0.04% on serializer version 2 and 7.6% on serializer version 3.
Within the version-3, compression-enabled cohort, failures occurred only when a serialized frame crossed a 64 KiB chunk boundary; many large payloads did not cross that boundary.
A staging replay using version 3 with compression disabled crossed the same chunk boundary 10,000 times without a checksum mismatch.
A staging replay using version 2 with compression enabled crossed the same chunk boundary 10,000 times without a checksum mismatch.
With version 3 and compression enabled, 317 of 10,000 boundary-crossing replays produced a cache payload shorter than the corresponding database payload.

For mismatching replays, the serializer's pre-compression byte count matched the database record, while the cache write's recorded compressed length was one chunk shorter than the compressor's output length.

The cache client logs its write as successful before a later read detects the checksum mismatch; current tracing does not capture the ownership or mutation of the output buffer between compression completion and cache write.

In a 5% canary that retained version 3 but disabled compression, new checksum mismatches stopped; the canary's cache bandwidth increased by 68% and p99 cache-write latency approached the client timeout.
In a separate 5% canary that retained compression but returned to version 2, new checksum mismatches stopped without a measurable bandwidth increase.
A dashboard shows a routine cache-library patch was installed three days earlier; aggregate checksum failure rates remained at baseline until the two rollout changes on the incident day.

hypotheses.text: Serializer version 3 is sufficient by itself to produce the elevated checksum failures.
Compression is sufficient by itself to produce the elevated checksum failures.
The elevated failures require the combination of serializer version 3 and compression under boundary-crossing payload conditions.
Primary-store corruption is the source of the mismatching payloads.
The cache-library patch changes output-buffer ownership in a way that contributes to the failures.

edges.relation: is sufficient to elevate checksum failures independently of compression
is sufficient to elevate checksum failures independently of serializer version
jointly creates the elevated checksum-failure condition
conditions whether the joint configuration can manifest the observed failure
supplies already-corrupted payloads to cache writes
changes buffer lifetime during cache writes

actions.text: Pause the version-3 rollout and route compression-enabled traffic to version 2 while preserving diagnostic samples.
Disable compression for every tenant while retaining version 3 on all instances.
Flush the entire distributed cache and immediately resume both rollout settings.
Add buffer-lifetime and length tracing around compression output and cache writes, then replay all four version-by-compression cohorts at chunk boundaries.
Scale the primary database to reduce its observed latency increase.
Revert the cache-library patch before conducting another controlled cohort test.
